message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 total), which is within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, is a buy order on an allowed ticker, and required no money movement out of the account (cash was $50,000). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year results reported October 31, 2024: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share — figures I verified against Apple's newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K filed November 1, 2024 (I disregarded a low-quality aggregator that misstated the units as millions). The growth return to positive year-over-year revenue, the $10.2 billion one-time tax charge being non-operational, and the pending Apple Intelligence rollout with iPhone 16 demand as the key swing factor supported a constructive but measured view, so I sized the position modestly rather than at the full $10,000 limit. The limit price of $223.00 was set just above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) to stay close to market while ensuring a fill.
